correctness.rationale: Sum the cited pointwise harmonic bound and use the nonpositive exact swap gains. Its guarantee decreases strictly with committee difference r, forcing r=k; equality then makes every swap and every per-voter slack vanish. With r≥2, the positive-increment estimate bounds slack below by (r−1)H_u/2−(r−1)/(u+1) when x≥y and x≥1, strictly positive for u>1. At u=1 equality requires x=y=1. The zero-additions and falling-score cases are strict for u>0, while u=0 requires x=0 or 1. Summing the neutral-swap equations by row forces equal row totals and then identical columns across rows. In the converse, with exactly 2k candidates, a committee containing t members of O with index set T has score kS+(t−1)(sum over T of d_t)/2, by counting pair approvals and subtracting half the double approvals. This confirms global optimality independently of the locality bound. The voter count is at least (3k−1)S/2. Nonnegative singleton counts require S≥(k+1)/2 for odd k, attainable with that many unit columns. For even k integrality forces each d_t even, so S≥k+1 implies S≥k+2, attained by (k+2)/2 columns of size two. Irrelevant voters cannot improve this minimum. No general converse with extra candidates is asserted.

value.rationale: The minimum number of voters is a natural measure of the size of an exact worst-case PAV instance, and the prior construction motivates minimizing it. The classification determines all distinct projected equality patterns, not just a smaller example, and explains the parity obstruction in the optimum. It can be used to generate sparse worst cases and to recognize why particular ballots cannot be extremal.
residual_risks: Exact, unweighted, one-swap regime only; neither near-equality stability nor an unrestricted extra-candidate converse follows.
